scope: Whole-tree structural inventory plus focused manual workflow review. This is not independent verification of every source line, historical result, or possible defect. Research records, originals, running state and GPU experiments were not changed.

environment.scientific_scope: CPU/synthetic checks only. No GPU memory-capacity measurement or original-data study rerun.

reproductions.method: Registration uses importable stand-in zarr/registration modules to reach the original false-success path. nnUNet uses a tiny real YAML at its fixed output path. The CPU memory search uses the actual CPU Torch runtime. The original main functions returned normally; their script entrypoints therefore reported success.

See docs/UNSUPPORTED_LAUNCHERS.md for the source and migration limits.

nnunet_bridge.stderr: This nnUNet bridge is retired. Inspect the pinned Villa segmentation/model_optimization_framework README and use an explicitly reviewed configuration for that separate workflow. See docs/UNSUPPORTED_LAUNCHERS.md for retained source and limits.

initial_regression_feature_selection.scope: Includes retirement/help/archive guards as well as bug regressions; not fifteen distinct defects.

validation.limits: The small CPU model test verifies real forward/backward. Allocator peak/reset, OOM cleanup and device-selection tests use a controlled fake backend, not physical CUDA measurements.

owner_review: The ten items in docs/REPOSITORY_AUDIT.md remain: dependency/Python/platform migrations; human-label feedback semantics; real source onboarding; representative GPU/ensemble profiling; package distribution scope; source-pinned scientific reruns; training read-failure policy; registration/adoption of v2 gates; archive/CI/dependency scope; legacy and experimental interfaces.

final_structural_inventory.scope: Whole-tree structural inventory of tracked regular files, not independent validation of all scientific results or source lines. Image checks are header/container checks; JSON nonfinite constants are recorded separately.
